world.title: Trump threatens to double Mexico tariffs over migrant caravan
world.summary: President Donald Trump threatened on Nov. 12 to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops a migrant caravan heading north, warning that its members would not be allowed into the United States. An estimated 1,500 people, mostly from Central America, set out from Tapachula near Guatemala on Tuesday. Trump linked their mov
world.content: President Donald Trump threatened on Nov. 12 to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops a migrant caravan heading north, warning that its members would not be allowed into the United States. An estimated 1,500 people, mostly from Central America, set out from Tapachula near Guatemala on Tuesday. Trump linked their movement to the U.S. midterm election results without providing evidence for that connection. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said no caravan had reached the U.S. border since Trump returned to office in January 2025. She said officials were explaining the difficulty of entering the United States and considering safe returns or conditional stays in Mexico. She also said there would be no repression. The two governments are negotiating trade arrangements after Trump declined in July to extend the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade pact.
world.image_alt: Trump threatens to double Mexico tariffs over migrant caravan

world.title: Kaliningrad court sentences rights lawyer Maria Bontsler to 12 years
world.summary: A court in Russia’s Kaliningrad region sentenced rights lawyer Maria Bontsler, 66, to 12 years in prison on treason charges, with an additional year of restrictions on her activities. Prosecutors alleged she passed information to Ukraine about regional security officers and criminal cases; they had sought a 15-year sen
world.content: A court in Russia’s Kaliningrad region sentenced rights lawyer Maria Bontsler, 66, to 12 years in prison on treason charges, with an additional year of restrictions on her activities. Prosecutors alleged she passed information to Ukraine about regional security officers and criminal cases; they had sought a 15-year sentence. Bontsler’s lawyers argued that the information was not secret and had been discussed in open court. The rights group Slovo Zashchite said the trial was held behind closed doors and that Bontsler and her chosen lawyers were barred from most proceedings. Independent Russian outlet Mediazona reported that the court removed her three retained lawyers and appointed a state defender. Bontsler has denied wrongdoing and said the case targets her legal work. The court issued the verdict on Nov. 12. A Czech report said it was not final and that Bontsler could appeal.
world.image_alt: Kaliningrad court sentences rights lawyer Maria Bontsler to 12 years

world.title: Yemen’s Houthis claim strikes on Saudi oil route as coalition intercepts drones
world.summary: Yemen’s Houthi movement said Thursday it attacked Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, an oil facility in Yanbu and a site belonging to oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh, as well as an airport and air base. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones over the Riyadh region and Eastern Province and destroyed m
world.content: Yemen’s Houthi movement said Thursday it attacked Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, an oil facility in Yanbu and a site belonging to oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh, as well as an airport and air base. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones over the Riyadh region and Eastern Province and destroyed missiles and drones elsewhere. It was unclear whether those interceptions matched the attacks the Houthis claimed. There were no immediate reports of damage to the Aramco site. The pipeline links Saudi oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted regional oil flows. Saudi Arabia said an earlier attack caused a fire at the pipeline on Monday but did not interrupt operations. On Thursday, the U.N. Security Council unanimously extended Yemen-related sanctions for a year, including asset freezes and travel bans, and renewed its demand that the Houthis stop attacks on Saudi Arabia.
world.image_alt: Yemen’s Houthis claim strikes on Saudi oil route as coalition intercepts drones

world.title: Truck crash and fire kill 14, injure 30 in UAE
world.summary: A truck crash and fire involving 23 vehicles killed 14 people and injured 30 shortly before midnight on Nov. 12 on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road near Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, authorities said. The truck driver lost control, struck another vehicle and overturned into vehicles stopped in slow-moving traffic. The t
world.content: A truck crash and fire involving 23 vehicles killed 14 people and injured 30 shortly before midnight on Nov. 12 on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road near Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, authorities said. The truck driver lost control, struck another vehicle and overturned into vehicles stopped in slow-moving traffic. The truck caught fire, and flames spread to other vehicles. Fifteen of the injured have been discharged from hospital, and 15 remain under treatment. The dead included Emirati nationals, and authorities are using DNA tests to identify some victims. Indian nationals were also among those killed. Police, ambulance and civil defence teams extinguished the fire, took the injured to hospitals and secured the scene. Fujairah Police said they are investigating the circumstances of the collision. The UAE Interior Ministry described the casualty figures as preliminary.
world.image_alt: Truck crash and fire kill 14, injure 30 in UAE

world.title: Iran claims it destroyed US radar in Bahrain after alleged Sirik strike
world.summary: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Friday it struck and destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar installation in Bahrain in retaliation for what it called an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, southern Iran. Neither the U.S. military nor Bahrain has confirmed a strike or damage, and the cl
world.content: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Friday it struck and destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar installation in Bahrain in retaliation for what it called an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, southern Iran. Neither the U.S. military nor Bahrain has confirmed a strike or damage, and the claim has not been independently verified. It was the first reported Iranian claim of an attack on U.S. military assets in a Gulf country since early September. The war began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28. Iran restricts shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and Washington maintains a naval blockade on Iranian ports. President Donald Trump said the United States no longer needs a deal, while the IRGC warned it was ready to respond without limits to any further actions it deemed violations. Trump has said U.S. forces remain ready to resume strikes. or Bahraini response to the radar claim.
world.image_alt: Iran claims it destroyed US radar in Bahrain after alleged Sirik strike

world.title: Israeli strike kills surgeon and child, disables key Gaza hospital wards
world.summary: An Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, one of Gaza’s main functioning hospitals, killed six people, including surgeon Rizk Abu Shaira and a 13-year-old boy, and injured at least 27, Palestinian health officials and the World Health Organization said. The strike hit the surgical department early Thursday d
world.content: An Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, one of Gaza’s main functioning hospitals, killed six people, including surgeon Rizk Abu Shaira and a 13-year-old boy, and injured at least 27, Palestinian health officials and the World Health Organization said. The strike hit the surgical department early Thursday during a ceasefire that began in October 2025. The hospital’s director, Dr. Ahmed al-Farra, said two missiles struck the building and one exploded. The damage halted surgeries and other services, including radiology and laboratory work. He said the hospital received no warning, while Israel’s military said it had issued warnings. The military said it targeted Hamas commander Muhammad Abu Ismail and other fighters it accused of using the complex as a headquarters. Abu Ismail’s name did not appear on the list of victims reported by the civil defence service, and the Israeli military did not say whether he was killed. The US-backed Board of Peace, which oversees the Gaza ceasefire plan, called for the plan’s immediate implementation after the attack.
world.image_alt: Israeli strike kills surgeon and child, disables key Gaza hospital wards

world.title: White House weighs Lutnick ouster as Congress probes Nvidia chip exports
world.summary: Senior White House officials are discussing whether to remove Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as lawmakers investigate the administration’s oversight of Nvidia’s advanced AI chip sales to China, according to people familiar with the discussions. President Donald Trump said publicly that he had “complete confidence” i
world.content: Senior White House officials are discussing whether to remove Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as lawmakers investigate the administration’s oversight of Nvidia’s advanced AI chip sales to China, according to people familiar with the discussions. President Donald Trump said publicly that he had “complete confidence” in Lutnick. No decision on Lutnick’s future was reported. Lawmakers are examining whether the Commerce Department delayed action against Singapore-based Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer whose executive Alice Huang is suspected by U.S. authorities of links to Chinese intelligence. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing; reports say it has bought more than $4.8 billion in Nvidia AI chips since June 2024. Lawmakers from both parties are questioning whether chips were diverted to Chinese buyers and whether the department adequately enforced export restrictions. Democratic senators have asked officials to preserve chip-export records, while lawmakers are considering bills to expand congressional oversight and restrict chip access through overseas data centers. Lutnick and Nvidia’s former chief executive, Jensen Huang, are expected to face congressional questioning. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said Huang would appear before his panel this month.
world.image_alt: White House weighs Lutnick ouster as Congress probes Nvidia chip exports

world.title: Pope Leo meets six abuse survivors, condemns violence against women in Peru
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV met six survivors of abuse by Catholic clergy and church institutions in Lima on Thursday and urged the Church to pursue truth, justice and reparation. Leo spent nearly two decades as a missionary and bishop in Peru. The Vatican said he spoke individually with each survivor for more than an hour; some had
world.content: Pope Leo XIV met six survivors of abuse by Catholic clergy and church institutions in Lima on Thursday and urged the Church to pursue truth, justice and reparation. Leo spent nearly two decades as a missionary and bishop in Peru. The Vatican said he spoke individually with each survivor for more than an hour; some had belonged to groups linked to Sodalitium Christianae Vitae, a Peruvian lay Catholic movement dissolved in 2025. Earlier Thursday, Leo told Peru’s bishops to accompany communities facing poverty and injustice and strengthen abuse prevention and protection. In a public address, he condemned “machismo” and violence against women, called for women to be valued, protected and respected, and noted that poor, Indigenous and Afro-Peruvian women face additional marginalization. Survivors and advocates pressed for remedies beyond listening, including financial help and a zero-tolerance approach to abusers. Leo is due to travel to Chiclayo on Friday, where he served as bishop from 2015 to 2023, before continuing to other parts of Peru.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo meets six abuse survivors, condemns violence against women in Peru

business.title: SpaceX targets first recovery of both Starship stages in 22-hour test
business.summary: SpaceX is targeting a Nov. 13 launch of its Starship Flight 15 test, aiming to catch both the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage at its Starbase site in Texas. The launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. Eastern, but the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration had not issued final approval as of late Thursday. If the fligh
business.content: SpaceX is targeting a Nov. 13 launch of its Starship Flight 15 test, aiming to catch both the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage at its Starbase site in Texas. The launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. Eastern, but the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration had not issued final approval as of late Thursday. If the flight proceeds, the booster would return minutes after launch; Ship would orbit Earth for about 22 hours before its planned catch attempt. SpaceX has caught the booster three times; this test would extend that effort to the faster, higher-flying upper stage. Ship is also set to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites. SpaceX says returning both stages to the launch site could shorten inspection and refurbishment before another flight.
business.image_alt: SpaceX targets first recovery of both Starship stages in 22-hour test

business.title: US lawmakers push tighter China chip curbs after Nvidia CEO exit
business.summary: U.S. lawmakers from both parties are pressing for tighter controls on exports of advanced artificial-intelligence chips to China after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned following reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia partner Megaspeed whom U.S. authorities suspect
business.content: U.S. lawmakers from both parties are pressing for tighter controls on exports of advanced artificial-intelligence chips to China after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned following reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia partner Megaspeed whom U.S. authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. China denies the allegation. House Speaker Mike Johnson said support for tighter limits was growing, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune said there was a “high probability” Congress would impose further restrictions. Republicans want new controls included in the annual defense authorization bill, but House and Senate negotiators have not agreed on the final text. The proposals would expand oversight of chip sales and address possible diversion through third countries or remote access to overseas computing capacity. Huang is expected to testify before Congress ahead of Thanksgiving, Nov. 26, while House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast’s staff discuss a date and location with Nvidia.
business.image_alt: US lawmakers push tighter China chip curbs after Nvidia CEO exit

business.title: Anthropic IPO demand reaches six times supply as allocations favor existing backers
business.summary: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering of 825 million shares has attracted orders for about six times the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter. Bankers have told prospective investors that existing backers of the Claude artificial-intelligence developer will receive priority, leaving some
business.content: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering of 825 million shares has attracted orders for about six times the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter. Bankers have told prospective investors that existing backers of the Claude artificial-intelligence developer will receive priority, leaving some other buyers with smaller allocations than requested. Demand could change, and the proposed valuation reaches $1.4 trillion. Anthropic seeks up to $64.4 billion in the IPO alongside a separate $26 billion private placement. The company expects to set its final share price on Nov. 18, with Nasdaq trading scheduled for Nov. 19 under the ticker ANT, subject to regulatory clearance.
business.image_alt: Anthropic IPO demand reaches six times supply as allocations favor existing backers

business.title: Inflation and borrowing fears drive Treasury yields higher again
business.summary: U.S. Treasury yields resumed climbing on Nov. 13 as persistent inflation, hawkish Federal Reserve signals and growing government debt supply kept bond investors braced for further rate increases. The selloff continued even as turmoil surrounding Nvidia weighed on stocks, weakening expectations that Treasuries would reg
business.content: U.S. Treasury yields resumed climbing on Nov. 13 as persistent inflation, hawkish Federal Reserve signals and growing government debt supply kept bond investors braced for further rate increases. The selloff continued even as turmoil surrounding Nvidia weighed on stocks, weakening expectations that Treasuries would regain their usual safe-haven appeal. U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, with core prices up 0.3% for a third consecutive month. India’s October retail inflation reached 6.09%, exceeding the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) 6% upper limit. Indian analysts say the data may shape expectations for the RBI’s Dec. 4 policy meeting, while global borrowing and inflation concerns continue to put upward pressure on long-term bond yields.
business.image_alt: Inflation and borrowing fears drive Treasury yields higher again

business.title: Gold rebounds from 13-month low as rate-hike bets pressure bullion
business.summary: Gold rose about 1% on Friday, Nov. 13, to roughly $3,915 an ounce after falling to its lowest level in more than a year in the previous session. It remained down about 3.5% for the week. Thursday’s selloff followed stronger U.S. inflation readings, rising Treasury yields and a stronger dollar, which increased expectati
business.content: Gold rose about 1% on Friday, Nov. 13, to roughly $3,915 an ounce after falling to its lowest level in more than a year in the previous session. It remained down about 3.5% for the week. Thursday’s selloff followed stronger U.S. inflation readings, rising Treasury yields and a stronger dollar, which increased expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates in December. Higher rates can weigh on gold because bullion does not pay interest. Investors were watching U.S. producer-price data due Friday for clues about inflation and the Fed’s next move. Dip buying and short-term market positioning contributed to gold’s rebound, according to market analysts. Silver also recovered on Friday but remained on course for a weekly loss.
business.image_alt: Gold rebounds from 13-month low as rate-hike bets pressure bullion

business.title: Singapore bars former Megaspeed executive as chip-routing investigation continues
business.summary: Singapore barred former Megaspeed chief executive Alice Huang from re-entering the country after warning her for knowingly giving police inaccurate information that downplayed her role at the company, the Ministry of Home Affairs said. Singapore said it found insufficient evidence that she committed offenses tied to su
business.content: Singapore barred former Megaspeed chief executive Alice Huang from re-entering the country after warning her for knowingly giving police inaccurate information that downplayed her role at the company, the Ministry of Home Affairs said. Singapore said it found insufficient evidence that she committed offenses tied to suspected false declarations and said its investigation did not concern espionage. Singapore opened its investigation in February 2025 into Megaspeed and other companies to determine whether servers sent through Singapore to Malaysia were accurately declared and later diverted elsewhere. Singapore held Huang’s passport from June 2025 until February 2026; she left after authorities returned it. The investigation into Megaspeed and six people remains open. Megaspeed says it has hired a U.S. law firm to inventory its graphics-processing units and independently review its export-control compliance. Singapore says it repeatedly sought U.S. assistance and information about server supplier Supermicro but received limited help. Supermicro denies selling products to Megaspeed, which has denied diverting chips.
business.image_alt: Singapore bars former Megaspeed executive as chip-routing investigation continues

business.title: U.S. existing-home sales fall 5.5% to lowest level since 2010
business.summary: Sales of previously owned U.S. homes fell 5.5% in October from September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million, the lowest pace since August 2010 and below economists’ forecasts. Sales were down 8.8% from a year earlier. Mortgage rates above 7%, elevated home prices and inflation have deterred buyers; ri
business.content: Sales of previously owned U.S. homes fell 5.5% in October from September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million, the lowest pace since August 2010 and below economists’ forecasts. Sales were down 8.8% from a year earlier. Mortgage rates above 7%, elevated home prices and inflation have deterred buyers; rising oil prices tied to the U.S.-Iran conflict have also pushed up bond yields and borrowing costs. The median existing-home price rose 0.4% year over year to $421,900, while distressed sales remained at 2%. Unsold inventory reached 1.59 million homes, equivalent to 5.1 months of supply, the highest level since November 2015. Economists expect mortgage rates to remain above 7% through much of 2027, with sales potentially staying below an annual pace of 4 million until late next year; markets were pricing in a Federal Reserve rate increase in December.
business.image_alt: U.S. existing-home sales fall 5.5% to lowest level since 2010

business.title: Nvidia shares slide as Huang exits, putting AI growth outlook under scrutiny
business.summary: Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% in early trading on Thursday, Nov. 12, after co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. The resignation followed reports about Huang’s personal relationships,
business.content: Nvidia shares fell as much as 14% in early trading on Thursday, Nov. 12, after co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent successor. The resignation followed reports about Huang’s personal relationships, including one with a woman U.S. officials suspect has links to Chinese intelligence. The stock recovered much of its intraday loss to close down about 4% to 5%, but remained more than 30% below its Oct. 6 record. Investors face leadership uncertainty and concerns about the pace of AI data-center spending. The sell-off has pushed Nvidia’s forward price-to-earnings ratio to about 12, its lowest level since 2012, while analysts still forecast a sharp rise in quarterly revenue and profit. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Nov. 17. Analysts forecast October-quarter revenue of about $109.2 billion and net profit above $60 billion.
business.image_alt: Nvidia shares slide as Huang exits, putting AI growth outlook under scrutiny

science.title: Alzheimer’s research revisits cholinergic loss and maps new disease pathways
science.summary: Recent Alzheimer’s research is examining mechanisms beyond amyloid plaques, including the loss of acetylcholine-producing neurons, tau spread and impaired transport of proteins from blood to the brain. A report in Science traces renewed interest in the cholinergic hypothesis, first articulated by researcher Raymond Bar
science.content: Recent Alzheimer’s research is examining mechanisms beyond amyloid plaques, including the loss of acetylcholine-producing neurons, tau spread and impaired transport of proteins from blood to the brain. A report in Science traces renewed interest in the cholinergic hypothesis, first articulated by researcher Raymond Bartus in 1982, while a large PET study found more widespread and faster-accumulating tau in patients whose symptoms began before age 65. In a Japanese cohort of 47,293 adults aged 65 or older, tooth loss was associated with higher dementia incidence, though the analysis does not establish that tooth loss causes dementia. A separate study in Alzheimer’s mouse models found that transport of protective blood proteins, including liver-derived APOA1, into the brain declined before the blood-brain barrier became physically leaky; raising APOA1 restored neuronal connectivity in those models. The mouse findings do not establish a treatment for people.
science.image_alt: Alzheimer’s research revisits cholinergic loss and maps new disease pathways

science.title: Space shuttle Endeavour opens in launch-ready display in Los Angeles
science.summary: The California Science Center is opening its space shuttle Endeavour exhibit to visitors on Nov. 13, with the shuttle displayed upright alongside its external tank and solid rocket boosters in a launch-ready configuration. The museum says it is the only place where visitors can see a complete shuttle stack assembled fr
science.content: The California Science Center is opening its space shuttle Endeavour exhibit to visitors on Nov. 13, with the shuttle displayed upright alongside its external tank and solid rocket boosters in a launch-ready configuration. The museum says it is the only place where visitors can see a complete shuttle stack assembled from real flight hardware. Endeavour arrived in Los Angeles in 2012 after completing 25 missions. The new Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center, built for the exhibit, cost $450 million. The new wing offers views of the shuttle from multiple levels and opens after more than a decade of construction.
science.image_alt: Space shuttle Endeavour opens in launch-ready display in Los Angeles

science.title: Webb and Gemini identify compact quasar pair from cosmic dawn
science.summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope and Gemini North have identified a close pair of quasar candidates, J1602+4228AB, as they appeared 900 million years after the Big Bang. Their black holes have estimated masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses and lie about 18,100 light-years apart, making the
science.content: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope and Gemini North have identified a close pair of quasar candidates, J1602+4228AB, as they appeared 900 million years after the Big Bang. Their black holes have estimated masses of 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses and lie about 18,100 light-years apart, making them the oldest known pair and the most compact pair found during cosmic dawn. Models struggle to explain how black holes grew so massive within the universe’s first billion years. Researchers spotted the fainter companion in Webb’s Aether survey and used Gemini North observations to distinguish the two objects. They have not definitively ruled out gravitational lensing, in which an intervening galaxy can make one object appear as two. A lens model is needed to settle that question.
science.image_alt: Webb and Gemini identify compact quasar pair from cosmic dawn

science.title: Europe’s Hera probe reveals Didymos ridge as asteroid-defense survey begins
science.summary: The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft has begun its close study of the Didymos asteroid pair. New images show boulders, craters and a sharply defined ridge around Didymos’ equator. Hera is inspecting the system after NASA deliberately struck its smaller moonlet, Dimorphos, in 2022 to test asteroid deflection. The
science.content: The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft has begun its close study of the Didymos asteroid pair. New images show boulders, craters and a sharply defined ridge around Didymos’ equator. Hera is inspecting the system after NASA deliberately struck its smaller moonlet, Dimorphos, in 2022 to test asteroid deflection. The images, taken from about 56 kilometers away, show a side of Didymos that NASA’s DART spacecraft did not see before impact. Scientists say Didymos’ rapid spin may help explain the ridge and could send surface material toward its equator or into space. Hera will continue its survey with 25 instruments. Two CubeSats are due to investigate Dimorphos at closer range, including with radar and an attempted landing. The agency plans to release detailed images of both asteroids on Nov. 25.
science.image_alt: Europe’s Hera probe reveals Didymos ridge as asteroid-defense survey begins

science.title: Study finds drought could cut cactus habitat by 80% by 2100
science.summary: An international research team analyzed nearly 1,000 cactus species and found that more than a quarter could lose at least 80% of their suitable habitat by 2100 if severe droughts intensify. The researchers added drought projections to climate models, which commonly use long-term temperature and rainfall averages, and
science.content: An international research team analyzed nearly 1,000 cactus species and found that more than a quarter could lose at least 80% of their suitable habitat by 2100 if severe droughts intensify. The researchers added drought projections to climate models, which commonly use long-term temperature and rainfall averages, and combined them with biodiversity records, field observations and community-science data. The projected losses could qualify affected species as Critically Endangered under criteria set by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), more than doubling the number of cacti in that category. Researchers say drought may also reduce growth or flowering without immediately killing plants, compounding threats from habitat destruction and illegal collection. The findings are expected to inform updated IUCN Red List assessments; the team says further research is needed to determine which life stages and biological processes drought affects.
science.image_alt: Study finds drought could cut cactus habitat by 80% by 2100

science.title: Monash researchers link Granzyme K to age-related organ damage
science.summary: Monash University researchers report that the immune-cell protein Granzyme K contributes to age-related damage in the heart, liver and kidneys, based on experiments in mice. Older mice lacking the protein had better heart function, less tissue scarring and fewer signs of liver and kidney damage. The study was published
science.content: Monash University researchers report that the immune-cell protein Granzyme K contributes to age-related damage in the heart, liver and kidneys, based on experiments in mice. Older mice lacking the protein had better heart function, less tissue scarring and fewer signs of liver and kidney damage. The study was published in Immunity. The findings do not establish that blocking Granzyme K would protect people. The mice lacked the protein throughout their lives, and the researchers say they still need to test whether blocking it later in life has similar effects. They are investigating ways to selectively block the protein, while further work is needed to determine whether the results apply to humans.
science.image_alt: Monash researchers link Granzyme K to age-related organ damage

science.title: Researchers will track marine life on sunken SS United States liner
science.summary: Researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution plan a multiyear study of the SS United States, the retired ocean liner deliberately sunk off Florida to form an artificial reef. The project will document how a marine community develops on the ship, with initial surveys planned within the first month after its N
science.content: Researchers at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution plan a multiyear study of the SS United States, the retired ocean liner deliberately sunk off Florida to form an artificial reef. The project will document how a marine community develops on the ship, with initial surveys planned within the first month after its Nov. 11 sinking. The team plans to collect water samples at 132 locations around the wreck and monitor microbial communities and marine life while tracking metals — including iron, manganese and nickel — released as the steel corrodes. Researchers say the development of a reef ecosystem is seldom observed from its earliest stages. The SS United States Preservation Foundation challenged the reef’s environmental safety before the sinking. It argued that deteriorating hull coatings could release chromium and zinc and that the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers had not fully assessed the environmental effects. A federal judge rejected its request to block the sinking on Nov. 6 but allowed it to refile.
science.image_alt: Researchers will track marine life on sunken SS United States liner

science.title: COP31 reports warn of faster warming as leaders dispute climate action
science.summary: Two assessments presented at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya warn that global warming is accelerating and current policies put the world on course for nearly 5°F (2.8°C) of warming by 2100. The European Union’s Copernicus climate service said warming could cross the Paris Agreement’s 2.7°F (1.5°C) threshold as soon
science.content: Two assessments presented at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya warn that global warming is accelerating and current policies put the world on course for nearly 5°F (2.8°C) of warming by 2100. The European Union’s Copernicus climate service said warming could cross the Paris Agreement’s 2.7°F (1.5°C) threshold as soon as 2029, compared with a projection of around 2045 when the pact was adopted. Leaders and negotiators called for stronger climate finance and resilience measures but remained divided over adaptation funding and phasing out fossil fuels. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said political consensus on climate action had “gone,” reaffirmed the UK’s 2050 net-zero target and appointed a climate security envoy. Campaigners challenged the pledge, citing the UK’s approval of the Jackdaw gas field and reduced support for heat pumps. Countries were asked to submit written comments on a proposed COP31 decision by Saturday.
science.image_alt: COP31 reports warn of faster warming as leaders dispute climate action

sports.title: England make 10 changes for Japan with World Cup places at stake
sports.summary: England head coach Steve Borthwick has made 10 changes to his starting XV for Saturday’s Nations Championship match against Japan at Twickenham, selecting back-row forward Henry Pollock, Bath centre Max Ojomoh and Gloucester winger Will Joseph. Pollock, 21, makes only his second England start; Ojomoh returns after near
sports.content: England head coach Steve Borthwick has made 10 changes to his starting XV for Saturday’s Nations Championship match against Japan at Twickenham, selecting back-row forward Henry Pollock, Bath centre Max Ojomoh and Gloucester winger Will Joseph. Pollock, 21, makes only his second England start; Ojomoh returns after nearly a year, while Joseph is set for his first England appearance since 2022. Northampton scrum-half Archie McParland could make his debut from the bench. Borthwick said the selection gives players a chance to press their claims for next year’s Rugby World Cup, but warned that the team’s performance must come first. England beat Australia 45-22 last weekend; Japan lost 28-21 to Wales. Injuries have also shaped the lineup: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is out for the rest of the autumn campaign, while England hope Ollie Chessum, George Furbank and Seb Atkinson can return for next Saturday’s match against New Zealand. England face Japan on 14 November at 16:40 GMT.
sports.image_alt: England make 10 changes for Japan with World Cup places at stake

sports.title: NBC assigns Jason Benetti to Notre Dame game after Dan Hicks dies
sports.summary: Dan Hicks, NBC Sports’ longtime golf and Olympics play-by-play announcer, died late Wednesday in Connecticut at 64 after an acute illness, his wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm, said Thursday. Hicks joined NBC in 1992 and became its lead golf announcer in 2000; he also called Olympic swimming and skiing and Notre Dame foo
sports.content: Dan Hicks, NBC Sports’ longtime golf and Olympics play-by-play announcer, died late Wednesday in Connecticut at 64 after an acute illness, his wife, ESPN anchor Hannah Storm, said Thursday. Hicks joined NBC in 1992 and became its lead golf announcer in 2000; he also called Olympic swimming and skiing and Notre Dame football. His broadcasts included Tiger Woods’ 2008 U.S. Open putt that forced a playoff. Hicks had been scheduled to call Notre Dame’s game against Boston College on Saturday. NBC has assigned announcer Jason Benetti to the broadcast. The network’s final Notre Dame game this season is scheduled for Nov. 21 against SMU, but NBC has not confirmed whether Benetti will call that game. Hicks is survived by Storm and their three daughters.

sports.content: Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez won Major League Baseball’s 2026 National and American League Most Valuable Player awards unanimously on Thursday, Nov. 12, each receiving all 30 first-place votes. Both won their first MVP awards, with Crow-Armstrong ending Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani’s two-year run as NL winner. Crow-Armstrong, 24, hit.280 with 45 home runs, 107 runs batted in and 41 stolen bases in all 162 games, joining the 40-homer, 40-steal club and winning a Gold Glove for his defense. Alvarez, 29, hit.316 with 42 homers and 106 RBIs, leading the majors in batting average, on-base percentage and slugging percentage. Alvarez played 158 games in 2026 after injuries limited him to 48 in 2025. This was the first year both league MVPs and both Cy Young winners received unanimous votes.

sports.content: Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 at San Siro on Thursday and move top of UEFA Nations League Group A1, with Francesco Pio Esposito scoring twice and Davide Frattesi adding a goal. France took a 10th-minute lead through Michael Olise after Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma gave the ball away. Esposito equalised before half-time, Frattesi put Italy ahead in the 63rd minute and Esposito converted a penalty 12 minutes later. Italy and France are level on 10 points, but Italy lead on head-to-head results. Belgium have nine points, leaving all three sides in contention for the two quarter-final places. The loss was France coach Zinedine Zidane’s first in charge. France struck the woodwork twice, while Italy’s Sebastiano Esposito missed a penalty before his brother Pio scored from the spot. The group concludes on Sunday, November 15, when Italy visit Belgium and France host Türkiye to decide the quarter-final places. Italy’s win also ended a 64-year wait for a home victory over France.

sports.content: Crystal Palace dismissed manager Pierre Sage on Nov. 12 after 16 matches and five months in charge, with the club bottom of the Premier League. A 3-1 home defeat by Liverpool on Nov. 8 was Palace’s fourth consecutive league loss; they had collected seven points from 10 games and conceded a league-high 24 goals. Sage’s record across all competitions was five wins, three draws and eight defeats. The club also parted ways with three members of Sage’s coaching staff. Palace sit 21st in the 36-team Europa League table after one win in four matches and have reached the Carabao Cup quarter-finals. Palace said they would provide an update on appointing a successor. Former Brentford and Tottenham manager Thomas Frank was in advanced talks, though no appointment had been confirmed. The team’s next league match is away to Coventry on Nov. 21.

sports.content: Australian fast bowler Mahli Beardman, 21, took 6-24 on his one-day international debut as England were dismissed for 131 in 33.4 overs in Perth on Friday. In the opening match of the three-game series, England lost seven wickets for 41 runs after reaching 24-1. At the latest reported score, Australia were 91-3 after 13 overs, needing 41 more runs to win with 37 overs remaining. Captain Mitchell Marsh made 50 from 30 balls, while Cooper Connolly added 27 before Jofra Archer dismissed him. Beardman’s haul surpassed the Australian debut record held by Tony Dodemaide since 1988. Spencer Johnson took 3-42, while Gus Atkinson top-scored for England with an unbeaten 29. The teams are due to meet next in Adelaide on Sunday, November 15, with the third ODI scheduled for Hobart on November 18.

sports.content: The Washington Commanders rallied to beat the New York Giants 24-21 at MetLife Stadium on Thursday as quarterback Jayden Daniels hit wide receiver Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Washington trailed 21-17 before getting the ball back when the Giants failed to run out the clock. Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards and three touchdowns but threw two fourth-quarter interceptions — his first of the season. Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy passed for a career-high 293 yards and connected with tight end Isaiah Likely for a 66-yard go-ahead touchdown. Cornerback Rasul Douglas intercepted McCarthy’s final pass to seal the win. The win lifted Washington to 3-5-1, two games behind the 5-3-1 Giants, and gave the Commanders the head-to-head tiebreaker after the teams’ earlier tie. Dallas can match New York’s win total by beating San Francisco on Sunday. Washington next hosts Cincinnati on Nov. 23, while the Giants next face Jacksonville.

sports.content: The Minnesota Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for quarterback Kirk Cousins before Tuesday’s deadline. Minnesota started 6-0 but has lost its last two games; in Monday’s 23-6 loss to Buffalo, Carson Wentz threw for 81 yards and committed three turnovers. Cousins had 2,340 passing yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions with Las Vegas this season. Cousins is expected to start Sunday against the Green Bay Packers after practicing with the first team, although Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell initially said the decision depended on whether Cousins felt ready. His return reunites him with receiver Justin Jefferson, who won NFL Offensive Player of the Year in their last full season together in 2022. Jefferson has 31 catches through Week 9 this year. The Vikings visit Green Bay at Lambeau Field on Nov. 15, seeking to complete a season sweep after winning the teams’ opener 39-22.
